name: Isolated Congenitally Uncorrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
aliases: Isolated Congenital Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries (uncorrected)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Cardiac MRI Diagnostic Criteria for CCTGA

criteria.description: Presence of atrioventricular discordance with morphological right atrium connected to morphological left ventricle and morphological left atrium connected to morphological right ventricle
Ventriculoarterial discordance with the aorta arising from the morphological right ventricle and pulmonary artery from the morphological left ventricle
No associated significant cardiac anomalies such as ventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, or tricuspid valve abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance confirmed by imaging modalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiography and cardiac MRI findings; absence of associated cardiac defects defines isolated form.

pathognomonic.notes: Defining anatomical feature rather than clinical symptom
Due to morphological right ventricle supporting systemic circulation
Conduction abnormalities common in isolated CCTGA

common.symptomName: Fatigue Related to Reduced Cardiac Output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac function
exhaustion related to poor heart pumping

common.symptomName: Murmur Due to Tricuspid Valve Regurgitation
searchTerms: noisy heart valve due to regurgitation

common.notes: Due to arrhythmias or conduction block

rare.notes: From atrial arrhythmias or intracardiac thrombus
Due to chronic right heart failure

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Normal routine blood counts and metabolic panels
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance
Cardiac MRI confirming morphological ventricular anatomy and function
Electrocardiogram showing conduction abnormalities including complete heart block
genetic: Rare familial cases reported but no definitive inheritance pattern
other: Electrophysiological studies may reveal conduction system disease

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of associated defects such as ventricular septal defect or pulmonary stenosis

redFlags: Complete heart block or high-grade atrioventricular block
Malignant ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac arrest
references: Graham TP Jr, Bernard YD, Mellen BG, et al. Long-term outcome in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries: a multi-institutional study. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2000;36(1):255-261.
